questions.q: What does Descartes do with any belief that can be doubted even slightly?
a: He abandons it and builds only on certainty
He keeps it until a better belief appears
He tests it by asking other philosophers
He treats it as true if it seems practical
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you cannot build understanding on lies, so anything doubtful must be set aside.

questions.q: Why does Descartes distrust the senses?
a: Dreams and illusions can feel completely real
Other people often describe things inaccurately
Scientific instruments are more reliable than eyes
The senses only work properly in daylight
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the vividness of dreams and fake images to show that what we perceive may not be real.

questions.q: What is the one thing Descartes finds he cannot doubt?
a: That he exists because he is thinking
That the physical world around him is real
That a benevolent God would not deceive him
That mathematics describes the universe perfectly
questions.why: Lesson 2 says even if the senses deceive us, the act of thinking proves that the thinker exists.

questions.q: Which level of truth does Descartes consider the most reliable?
a: Truths explained using only the mind, such as mathematics
Truths based on direct observation with the senses
Truths that combine imagination with sensory experience
Truths accepted on the authority of respected teachers
questions.why: Lesson 3 says mind-only truths are the most sound because thinking is our most reliable faculty.

questions.q: What are third-level truths like dragons and fairies, according to Descartes?
a: Combinations of mind and senses that have little reality
Direct perceptions that are as reliable as math
Purely mental constructs with no sensory element
Religious truths that reason cannot examine
questions.why: Lesson 3 places mixtures of mind and senses, such as mythical creatures, in the least reliable category.
